 Ventura County sees steady rain as storm moves into Southern California 
 Ventura County was among the first areas in Southern California to see rainfall Wednesday, with rain beginning around 8:30 a.m. By Sid Garcia Wednesday, October 21, 2026 10:15PM Share VENTURA, Calif. (KABC) -- Ventura County was among the first areas in Southern California to see rainfall Wednesday, with rain beginning around 8:30 a.m.
 The rain was visible along the northbound 101 Freeway in Camarillo, where wet conditions greeted drivers during the morning commute.
 Many residents welcomed the rain.
 "I love it, we need it. We still gotta get our toes done though. Going for a pedicure, I had to get rid of the Dodger blue," said Janet Jung of Ventura.
 Ventura County Fire officials said they have additional personnel on hand over the next couple of days to monitor rainfall in burn areas and other vulnerable spots in Ventura County.
 "What we're concerned about is the possibility of significant impacts to some isolated areas throughout the county," said Andrew Dowd of the Ventura County Fire Department. "We're not talking about a widespread event where we're gonna see downpouring rain that lasts days and days, but we could see rainfall amounts that exceed critical thresholds for possible localized flooding."
 The rain remained steady and mostly light throughout the day, with no heavy downpours. Residents and visitors alike said they hoped conditions would remain manageable.
 "Well of course Nature is a very powerful thing and I think we can just be respectful of it, you know. So I'm just out here looking at the awesomeness of the water and the ocean... along with this rain. Such a dramatic change in the last few days," said Sonya Perry of Pasadena.
 Officials will continue monitoring conditions as rain moves through Ventura County and other parts of Southern California. Drivers are urged to take safety precautions due to slick roadways and give themselves extra time to get to their destinations, as well as be aware of their surroundings when driving through recent burn areas.
